newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end up, look to U.S. jobless.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end up, look to U.S. jobless.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Thursday, supported by a fourth straight day of gains in U.S. Treasuries.
"The market remains strong," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/8 at 95-1/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.08 at 118.85.

The market was boosted by a U.S. second-quarter gross domestic product report showing 2.2 percent in the quarter. That was slightly above expectations but there were market-friendly downward revisions to first quarter growth to 4.9 percent from 5.9 percent.
Traders said the market continued to be well bid but many players express concern at the market's high levels.
"We are arriving at profit-taking levels but we are rolling on the trend," said another trader.
Still, there are factors warranting more gains as well, said the trader, such as the possibility of an upgrade in Argentina's credit rating by Moody's Investors Service.
Traders said on Friday the main focus is set to be the release of U.S. jobless figures.
In the money markets, the three-month peso BAIBOR, the Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, was flat at 7.0625 percent.
